intro: EHN Guardians Nanaimo is EHN Canada's inpatient trauma and addiction centre on Vancouver Island for Canadian Armed Forces members, veterans, RCMP officers and other first responders. It treats PTSD, operational stress injuries and moral injury, with or without a substance use problem, and it takes no civilian clients.

The centre is at 2113 Boxwood Road in Nanaimo, on the campus it shares with EHN Edgewood Nanaimo. Guardians clients live in a separate, self-contained building with private rooms, and clinicians' offices sit next door to where clients sleep and eat. Physicians and psychiatrists lead the programs, with nurses on site 24/7.

pillars.title: Trauma Therapy With or Without Addiction Care
pillars.body: Guardians Nanaimo runs two inpatient tracks. The 7-week trauma, PTSD and psychological injury program is for people whose main struggle is an operational stress injury. The 9-week trauma, PTSD and addiction program adds medically supervised detox when it's needed, relapse prevention and work on recovery skills. Both use cognitive processing therapy, prolonged exposure, CBT, DBT and Internal Family Systems, with a primary counsellor you see at least once a week and peer groups on symptoms, emotions and going back to work.

pillars.title: A Separate Building on a Wooded Nanaimo Campus
pillars.body: The program has its own quiet building on Boxwood Road, set apart from the civilian patients at EHN Edgewood Nanaimo. EHN calls it a refuge for clients who feel triggered or dysregulated. Every bedroom is private. Clients share the larger campus for meals in the Bridges Dining Room, the café, the gym, the wooded trails and an outdoor labyrinth used for walking meditation.

pillars.title: A Year of Alumni Groups After Discharge
pillars.body: After discharge, clients go on to a weekly therapy group with other alumni for one year, where they go back over the skills they learned and talk through what is getting hard. They also get lifelong membership in the EHN Canada Alumni Association, and aftercare and relapse prevention groups run both in person and online, which is handy for clients who go home to the mainland or further.

overview: The centre is built for people whose trauma comes from the job. Admission requires a primary diagnosis tied to an operational stress injury, and every client is a military member, veteran, first responder or someone covered by presumptive PTSD or OSI legislation. In the sample day EHN publishes, the evening is given over to trauma peer groups with other guardians, on topics like managing symptoms and going back to work.

location.heading: EHN Guardians Nanaimo in Nanaimo, British Columbia
location.intro: EHN Guardians Nanaimo is on Boxwood Road in central Nanaimo, on the east coast of Vancouver Island and about 10 minutes from the Departure Bay ferry terminal. From Vancouver the trip takes about three hours including the Horseshoe Bay ferry, Victoria is roughly an hour and a half south over the Malahat, and Parksville, Ladysmith and Duncan in the Cowichan Valley are all under an hour away by car.

faqIntro: Answers come from the EHN Canada website and public listings. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: Who can attend EHN Guardians Nanaimo?
faqs.a: EHN Guardians Nanaimo is only for people in uniformed and protective roles: Canadian Armed Forces members, veterans, RCMP officers, municipal and provincial first responders, and others covered by presumptive PTSD or operational stress injury legislation. The program pages also list healthcare professionals. The main diagnosis has to relate to an operational stress injury, with or without a substance use problem.

faqs.q: Is EHN Guardians Nanaimo the same as EHN Edgewood Nanaimo?
faqs.a: No. Both are run by EHN Canada and share a campus on Boxwood Road in Nanaimo, but Guardians is a separate program for military, veterans and first responders. Guardians clients live in their own building away from civilian patients, while they can still use shared campus spaces like the dining room, café and gym.

faqs.q: How long are the programs at EHN Guardians Nanaimo?
faqs.a: The trauma, PTSD and psychological injury program runs 7 weeks. The trauma, PTSD and addiction program, for people who also struggle with alcohol or drugs, runs 9 weeks. EHN says extended care is available for some clients.

faqs.q: How much does EHN Guardians Nanaimo cost?
faqs.a: EHN does not publish prices for Guardians Nanaimo. The admissions team gives you a cost after a free assessment confirms the program fits. EHN says the cost depends on program length, clinical complexity and your needs.

faqs.q: Can Veterans Affairs, WorkSafeBC or the RCMP pay for treatment?
faqs.a: Often, yes. EHN says it works with Veterans Affairs Canada, WorkSafeBC and RCMP Health Services, and that private and group health insurance may also be used. The admissions team checks your eligibility and handles the claims with you.

faqs.q: Does EHN Guardians Nanaimo offer medical detox?
faqs.a: Yes. Medically supervised detox and stabilization are part of admission when they are clinically needed. Nurses and counsellors are on site 24/7 and doctors are available.

No referral is needed. You do need to be a military member, veteran or first responder, and an admissions coordinator talks with you first to check that the program is a good fit. Complex cases are reviewed one by one by the clinical team.

The core therapies are cognitive processing therapy, prolonged exposure (including exposures done with occupational therapists), EMDR, CBT, DBT and Internal Family Systems, plus individual and group therapy. Days also include trauma-sensitive yoga, therapeutic boxing, art therapy, virtual reality, sound therapy and forest bathing.

faqs.q: Where is EHN Guardians Nanaimo and how do I get there?
faqs.a: The centre is at 2113 Boxwood Road in central Nanaimo, on the east coast of Vancouver Island and about 10 minutes from the Departure Bay ferry terminal. From Vancouver it takes about three hours including the Horseshoe Bay ferry, and Victoria is roughly an hour and a half south by car.

faqs.q: What support is there after the program?
faqs.a: After discharge you join a weekly therapy group with other alumni for one year. You also get lifelong membership in the EHN Canada Alumni Association, and aftercare and relapse prevention groups run both in person and online.
Google lists the centre's hours as Monday to Friday, 8 am to 8 pm, and Saturday and Sunday, 8:30 am to 6 pm. You can also send an inquiry through the EHN Canada website at any time.
